propositions: materialize_tickets writes a complete fresh copy of the ~620 MiB ticket tree on every gate resolution despite adjacent SHAs differing by only 1-3 files, producing ~10^5x write amplification with no reuse of the content-addressed cache key

the tickets-<sha> key advances every ~26 seconds (1,374 commits in 10 hours with ~1 file changed per commit), so the dest.is_dir() cache-hit branch is never reached in practice, turning the bounded cache into an append-only log
concurrent agents materializing gates multiply the per-resolution disk I/O directly, correlating with measured sustained 4.4 GiB/h disk growth and potential CPU starvation during multi-agent testing

the accounting for shared inodes was incomplete: entry_size summed st_size per file without inode deduplication, and _evict credited a free-space watermark with bytes still on disk when entries hardlink, worsening the original symptom

hardlinking all unchanged paths against the prior tickets entry and rewriting only differing paths via delta_tree recovers the cache-hit semantic while preserving content-addressed integrity (all materialized paths match git ls-tree and git show)

test mutations (M1–M8) on independent accounting sides demonstrate that the fix's three size concepts (entry_size for reporting, exclusive_size for populate/evict increments, distinct_bytes for sweep ground truth) are necessary and sufficient to prevent silent over-crediting of freed bytes
